name: Huggy Bear
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Five people from Brighton promised to last three years, then turned down the major labels, the photographs and most of the interviews, and split on schedule.

eras.title: Girl-boy revolutionaries
eras.text: Huggy Bear formed in Brighton in 1991, women and men together, and called themselves girl-boy revolutionaries. Their first records came out on Wiiija in 1992, and the major labels were already bidding.

years.cap: Huggy Bear in their five-piece line-up
years.h: Opening for Heavenly, five strangers to the stage
years.p: Niki Eleni, [[Jo Johnson|5c306572-a722-4e91-bbcf-e93f06cee73e]], Karen Hill, Chris Rowley and [[Jon Slade|c749b05c-ce7a-47ba-bd6b-6d3790c6ec34]] play their first show as support to Heavenly, per AllMusic.
years.xp:
AllMusic has Heavenly as the headliner for the first show. The exact date and venue aren't in the sources we found.

The photo shows the five-piece with Slade, who was in the band until early 1994.

years.h: Rubbing the Impossible to Burst, 2,000 copies on Wiiija 16
years.p: The debut 7-inch on Wiiija mixes shouted punk with tape collage, in a limited run of 2,000.
years.xp: AllMusic describes the record as musical rants and tape pastiches carrying a political message. Wikipedia lists the 2,000-copy limit for the 7-inch.

years.h: Major labels bid for Huggy Bear. The band stays on Wiiija
years.p: After Wiiija collects early demos, AllMusic reports a major-label bidding war. The band says no.
years.xp: The band also declined interviews and photographs for most of its life and kept its full names off the record, according to AllMusic and Wikipedia. It was a house rule, not a stunt for the press to solve.

years.h: Kiss Curl for the Kid's Lib Guerrillas closes the year
years.p: A second 7-inch on Wiiija (No. 18) lands three months after the debut.

eras.title: The Word, and everything after
eras.text: In 1993 Huggy Bear meets Bikini Kill, plays live network TV and gets escorted off it. The British music press turns riot grrrl into a story, and the band keeps putting out records.

years.big: "Her Jazz" on The Word, Valentine's Day
yt: Her Jazz on The Word, February 14, 1993
years.h: Live on Channel 4, then out the door
years.p: Huggy Bear play "Her Jazz" on Channel 4's The Word, then protest a segment on the Barbi Twins and are ejected.
years.xp: After the performance the band and friends shouted at presenter Terry Christian over the Barbi Twins item, and security removed them. A show spokesperson said someone had bitten the face of a production staffer. John Robb, who was there, disputed that, saying no biting happened and security was heavy-handed. Melody Maker compared the row to the Sex Pistols and Bill Grundy.

years.h: Bikini Kill cross the Atlantic to tour with Huggy Bear
years.p: [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]]'s band joins Huggy Bear on a British tour, which Ngaire Ruth's history of riot grrrl calls pivotal in bringing the scene to Britain.
years.xp: Ruth writes about the tour in Loud Women's history of riot grrrl, and AllMusic also connects the two bands. Tour dates aren't given in the sources we found.

years.big: So simple, so ugly, so daring.
yt: Our Troubled Youth, Huggy Bear side
years.h: Split with Bikini Kill, out on International Women's Day
years.p: Our Troubled Youth pairs Huggy Bear's eight songs with Bikini Kill's Yeah Yeah Yeah Yeah. Bloc Party's Gordon Moakes later called "Blow Dry" formative.
years.xp:
Huggy Bear's side comes out on Catcall Records in the UK and Kill Rock Stars in the US, and runs to eight songs, including "Blow Dry", "Hopscotch" and "February 14th". NME's Lisa Wright called it a more perfect teenage punk album you will not find.

The pull line is Moakes on "Blow Dry".

years.h: Taking the Rough with the Smooch gathers the early singles
years.p: The compilation on Kill Rock Stars and Wiiija collects the early recordings for listeners outside the UK.

years.h: Jo and Niki start Blood Sausage with a poet
years.p: [[Blood Sausage|bb52564b-068a-4dda-9214-6429f98e01ff]] is a side project with Dale Shaw, and its Touching You in Ways That Don't Feel Comfortable EP is NME Single of the Week.

eras.title: Three years, as promised
eras.text: The band always said it would last three years. In 1994 the line-up drops to four, the one album arrives, and the last show closes the year.

years.cap: Huggy Bear as a four-piece, 1994: Johnson in front, Rowley, Niki Elliott and Hill behind
years.h: Jon Slade leaves, and four are left
years.p: [[Jon Slade|c749b05c-ce7a-47ba-bd6b-6d3790c6ec34]] leaves in early 1994, per Wikipedia, and later joins [[Comet Gain|65cc77e1-45cf-4c2a-958c-c7cca472970c]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Weaponry Listens to Love · AllMusic
years.h: Weaponry Listens to Love, the only album, comes out heavier
years.p: Released on Wiiija in the UK and Kill Rock Stars in the US, with Slade gone. AllMusic hears more male lead vocals than before.
years.xp: Reviews were mixed. The Guardian said it was as enraged as the first but lacked its modulating whimsy; The Rocket called it brutal, harsh and chilling; NME gave it 6 out of 10. Tracks include "Immature Adolescence" and "Facedown".

years.cap: Niki Elliott with Graham Coxon of Blur, 1994
years.h: Huggy Bear break up in December, on the three-year plan
years.p: Wikipedia places the split shortly after a North American tour. The band had said from the start it would last three years.

eras.title: Killed (Of Kids)
eras.text: The members spend the years between in other bands. In 2024 a book collects everything Huggy Bear made, and three of them play together for the first time in thirty years.

years.p: With members of Male Bonding, Rowley releases County Pride in 2020 on What's Your Rupture? Karen Hill's [[Phantom Pregnancies|2973b718-e4ec-49ac-b116-9d611a343474]] and Jo Johnson's ambient records are others.

years.h: All seven zines, 352 pages, one book
years.p: Killed (Of Kids), from JABS and The Grass Is Green In The Fields For You, holds the band's zines, photos, flyers and new interviews with all five members.
years.xp: At the book launch at New River Studios, Hill, Slade and Rowley performed together for the first time in thirty years, according to Wikipedia.

sources.title: Loud Women: What did riot grrrl ever do for us? Part 2
